evals.prompt: During a product launch, our Redis OSS ElastiCache cluster shows host `CPUUtilization = 24%` while **`EngineCPUUtilization = 98%`**, `Evictions` jumped to `15,000/min`, and simultaneously expiring hero-banner cache keys are hammering our Aurora writer with a thundering herd. Diagnose both metrics and remediate.
evals.expected_output: Loads `references/elasticache-and-sqs-dlq.md` and diagnoses both failure modes: (1) Valkey/Redis core command execution is single-threaded, so `EngineCPUUtilization = 98%` means the main event loop is saturated (even when multi-vCPU host `CPUUtilization` is `24%`) due to `KEYS *`, heavy Lua, or a hot key — replace `KEYS` with `SCAN`, offload reads to replicas, and upgrade to ElastiCache for Valkey (multi-threaded I/O); and (2) stop `Evictions` & Cache Stampede by right-sizing memory / `allkeys-lfu` (`volatile-lru`), adding randomized TTL jitter (`TTL + random(0..60s)`), and implementing singleflight / distributed mutex lock (or probabilistic early recomputation) on cache misses.
expectations: Activates the database-and-cache-reliability skill

Distinguishes single-threaded `EngineCPUUtilization` (`98%`) from multi-core host `CPUUtilization` (`24%`), replacing `KEYS *` with `SCAN` and recommending ElastiCache for Valkey / replica read offload
Mitigates `Evictions` and thundering-herd Cache Stampede using randomized TTL jitter, singleflight/distributed lock coalescing, and `allkeys-lfu` / memory scaling

evals.prompt: A traffic spike scaled AWS Lambda to `1,500` concurrent containers, crashing Aurora PostgreSQL with `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections`, and on our staging RDS Proxy `DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned` is `80%`. Fix both.
evals.expected_output: Loads `references/aurora-rds-diagnostics.md`: (1) place Amazon RDS Proxy between Lambda and Aurora (with IAM auth / Secrets Manager pooling and bounded `MaxConnectionsPercent`) so `1,500` ephemeral containers share a compact backend pool without exhausting `max_connections`; and (2) fix `80%` `DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned` (`>50%` disables multiplexing!) by eliminating session-level `SET` statements (moving them to DB Parameter Groups or Proxy `InitQuery`), disabling driver-level named prepared statements (`prepare_threshold`), and avoiding `CREATE TEMP TABLE`.
expectations: Activates the database-and-cache-reliability skill
Places Amazon RDS Proxy (with bounded `MaxConnectionsPercent`) in front of Aurora to absorb the 1,500-container Lambda connection storm
Diagnoses `80%` `DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned` (>50% threshold) and removes session `SET` commands / prepared statements / temp tables

evals.prompt: Downstream Aurora lock contention caused our SQS order-worker Lambda to time out at `30s` (queue `VisibilityTimeout` is also set to `30s`), driving `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` to `52 minutes` and dumping `40,000` messages into the Dead-Letter Queue. Give the exact stabilization and DLQ redrive sequence.
evals.expected_output: Loads `references/elasticache-and-sqs-dlq.md` and enforces safe recovery ordering: (1) fix the VisibilityTimeout mismatch FIRST — set SQS `VisibilityTimeout >= 6 × Lambda function timeout` (`>= 180s` + batch jitter) so slow in-flight messages aren't delivered twice concurrently; (2) resolve the downstream Aurora lock bottleneck (`pg_blocking_pids` / `Lock:transactionid`) and cap Lambda ESM `MaximumConcurrency` so consumers don't overwhelm the DB; and (3) ONLY AFTER downstream health is verified, run `sqs:StartMessageMoveTask` with a conservative `MaxNumberOfMessagesPerSecond` rate limit (and idempotent consumer handling) so `40,000` DLQ messages don't re-saturate Aurora and bounce back to the DLQ.
expectations: Activates the database-and-cache-reliability skill
Fixes `VisibilityTimeout` from `30s` (`1x`) to `>= 180s` (`>= 6x` the 30s Lambda timeout) and resolves downstream Aurora contention / caps ESM `MaximumConcurrency` first
Runs rate-limited `StartMessageMoveTask` (`MaxNumberOfMessagesPerSecond`) only AFTER downstream database stability is restored

evals.prompt: During Aurora Multi-AZ failovers, our Java Spring Boot and Python services suffer `45–65 seconds` of failed requests due to JVM/OS DNS caching and stale socket pools. How do we cut application failover recovery down to `3–8 seconds`?
evals.expected_output: Prescribes Section 2.2 (Fast Failover RTO Reduction): (1) adopt the AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper (`software.amazon.jdbc`) for Java and `aws-advanced-python-wrapper` for Python, which poll Aurora cluster topology metadata directly (`aurora_replica_status()` / `replica_host_status`), bypass stale DNS TTLs, detect writer promotion immediately, and switch active connections in `3–8 seconds` (paired with aggressive JVM `networkaddress.cache.ttl=1` and short connect/socket timeouts); and (2) optionally combine with Amazon RDS Proxy for sub-second connection queuing across failovers.
expectations: Activates the database-and-cache-reliability skill
Recommends the AWS Advanced JDBC / Python Wrapper Driver querying Aurora cluster topology directly to cut failover recovery from 45-60s DNS TTL down to 3-8 seconds
Tunes DNS cache TTL (`networkaddress.cache.ttl=1` / socket connect timeouts) and notes RDS Proxy fast failover integration

evals.prompt: Our checkout API is returning `503` errors because DynamoDB `PutItem` calls on `Orders` are failing with `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` even though `Orders` is at `20%` provisioned WCU — meanwhile `OrdersByMerchantDateGSI` shows `OnlineIndexThrottleEvents > 5,000/min` and `OnlineIndexConsumedWriteCapacity` pegged at `100%`. Explain the cascading failure and immediate + permanent fixes.
evals.expected_output: Loads `references/dynamodb-throttling-and-gsi.md`: explains GSI Write Backpressure — asynchronous replication from base table to GSI uses an internal buffer; when an under-provisioned or hot-partitioned GSI (`OrdersByMerchantDateGSI` pegged at 100% / >1,000 WCU on one merchant partition) fills that buffer, DynamoDB throttles writes on the base `Orders` table to prevent unbounded lag! Immediate mitigation: raise GSI provisioned WCU `>=` base table write amplification (or switch to On-Demand + Warm Throughput) and enable Contributor Insights; permanent fix: additive write-sharded GSI key (`MERCHANT#<id>#<shard>`) and sparse/minimal GSI projection.
expectations: Activates the database-and-cache-reliability skill and references GSI write backpressure mechanics
Explains how an exhausted GSI replication buffer (`OnlineIndexThrottleEvents`) throttles base-table `PutItem` writes even when base WCU is at 20%
Provides immediate mitigation (raise GSI WCU >= base write volume / On-Demand + Contributor Insights) and permanent additive write-sharded GSI key design

evals.prompt: On our Aurora MySQL cluster, `AuroraReplicaLag` spikes to `8,000 ms` during bulk batch updates, causing reader instances to restart from buffer-pool eviction pressure and serving stale data to users right after checkout.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses Aurora shared-storage page invalidation & reader lag: heavy bulk writer updates flood the shared storage log stream faster than undersized readers can apply page invalidations (if lag exceeds buffer bounds, Aurora restarts the reader to resync!). Fixes: (1) size HA/production readers to match the writer instance class (`PromotionTier 0–1`) and chunk bulk updates into small rate-limited batches (`1,000` rows + brief pause); (2) route read-after-write critical checkout confirmation queries to the Writer endpoint (or use session causal tokens); and (3) alarm on `AuroraReplicaLag` / `AuroraReplicaLagMaximum`.
expectations: Activates the database-and-cache-reliability skill
Explains how unthrottled bulk writer updates overwhelm undersized Aurora readers with storage/cache invalidations (risking reader restarts when lag grows excessive)
Prescribes matching reader instance sizing, batch-chunking bulk writes, and routing read-after-write critical reads to the Writer endpoint
